content.text: Finite-horizon scalar LQR uses backward Riccati recursion. For a scalar discrete plant `x[k+1]=a x[k]+b u[k]`, consider a finite-horizon quadratic objective `Σ(q x[k]²+r u[k]²)+q_f x[N]²` with q and q_f nonnegative and r strictly positive. The optimal unconstrained policy under this exact model is `u[k]=−K[k] x[k]`, obtained from backward scalar Riccati recursion. With `S[N]=q_f`, `K[k]=b S[k+1] a/(r+b² S[k+1])`, `S[k]=q+a² S[k+1]−a b S[k+1]K[k]`. Domain context: 10_finite_horizon_optimal_control_and_constraints.md. A declared model is not a validated hardware controller.
uncertainty: No experimentally calibrated parameter uncertainty or sensor covariance verified
units: Model quantities and time units must be explicitly declared; scalar educational values are not measured

gaps: No experiment on actual controller, sensor, actuator or agent
